title: Jitter Harmonics — Latency & Cost Playbook
content:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This note captures a compact experimental playbook and first-pass results for measuring and explaining short-timescale latency jitter ("harmonics") and its interaction with per-token cost under three inference configurations. The goal is pragmatic: give product and runtime teams a reproducible test shape + interpretable table to help choose default knobs for interactive SLAs.

Key takeaway (short): jitter "harmonics" from small microbursts amplifies p99 more than average throughput; quantization cuts steady-state cost but increases jitter amplitude for bursty arrivals. Hybrid (prefetch + int8 on-cold path) reduces cost while keeping p90 close to baseline; p99 still needs routing/pacing mitigations.

---
EXPERIMENT SETUP (replicable)
- Workload: chat-style sessions with 70% short-turns (prompt 50-150 tokens, reply 20-120 tokens), 30% long-turns (reply 200-800 tokens). Inter-arrival: Poisson baseline with injected microbursts (100 requests in 3s window) every 5 minutes.
- Models & configs tested:
  * baseline-fp16 — standard fp16 runtime (no extra prefetching), continuous batching enabled (batch cap 32), KV cache enabled.
  * int8-quant — int8 quantized model, same batching, lowered kernel parallelism to reduce mem pressure.
  * hybrid-prefetch — int8 quant for new tokens but aggressive prefetching of KV for active sessions + opportunistic small-batch coalescing (tiling), slight increase in concurrency slots.
- Hardware: A100 80GB (prod-sim), measured on dedicated pool with synthetic clients.
- Duration: 6 hours per run (to observe multiple bursts).
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p99 tail latencies (ms) for response-first-byte, token throughput, cost estimate ($ / 1k tokens) computed from GPU-minutes used + mem footprint amortization. Also captured jitter waveform at 100ms granularity.

---
RAW SUMMARY TABLE (single-number snapshot, median across runs)

Config                 | p50 (ms) | p90 (ms) | p99 (ms) | est $ / 1k tokens
-----------------------|----------|----------|----------|------------------
baseline-fp16          |  28      |   78     |  220     | 0.45
int8-quant             |  36      |   110    |  340     | 0.27
hybrid-prefetch        |  31      |   85     |  260     | 0.33

Notes on table: p50 is fairly insensitive to quantization; p99 amplifies under int8 due to long-tail kernel stalls during bursts. hybrid-prefetch trades a small cost increase vs int8 for p99 improvement.

JITTER HARMONICS DECOMPOSITION (qualitative)
- Observed microbursts create a clear two-tone pattern in the 0.5–2s and 5–10s bands.
- int8-quant shows higher amplitude at the 0.5–2s band (short kernel contention spikes).
- baseline-fp16 spreads energy across longer frequencies (queueing + KV fetchs).
- hybrid reduces the 0.5–2s band by prefetching KV but leaves a residual 5–10s tail from admission control fallbacks.

INTERPRETATION / CHEAT SHEET (for product conversations)
- If customer prioritizes p50/p90 interactive feel and absolute $/1k tokens: int8 gives best steady cost but expect worse p99 under heavy microburst patterns. Recommend hybrid as default for self-serve where tail-sensitive workloads are common.
- If customer buys Dedicated with high concurrency guarantees (reserved slots), int8 is attractive — pair with slot-pacing to mitigate bursts.
- For Private deployments: more conservative defaults (fp16 or hybrid) unless customer validates int8 under their traffic shape.

OPERATIONAL KNOBS (what we can expose in Console)
- "burst_pacing" boolean: enable slot-based admission during microburst detection.
- "kv_prefetch_aggressiveness": 0..3 (higher reduces p99 but uses memory).
- "quantization_mode": off|warm|aggressive (warm = hybrid fallback to fp16 on tail events).
- "microburst_detector_window_ms": default 3000 (tunable).

REPROD CHECKLIST (for SRE + bench infra)
- Reuse bench harness PR #233 (linked).
- Make sure GPU throttling disabled.
- Log raw 100ms buckets for 6-hour runs.
- Tag runs with traffic-seed and microburst-txid.

OPEN QUESTIONS / NOTES TO SELF
- Need to validate across GPU families (A100 vs H100 vs NVIDIA L4) — quantized kernel behavior differs.
- Cost calc has approximations for memory-amortized footprint; run a sensitivity table for mem-price allocation.
- Could KV prefetch + lightweight admission reduce p99 below baseline while keeping cost near int8? initial hybrid suggests partial win but more tuning needed.
- Investigate kernel-level stall accounting (probe nvprof/trace) during int8 p99 spikes.

NEXT STEPS (short roadmap)
1) Run same suite on H100 (1 week).
2) Add slot-pacing + adaptive throttling to hybrid run (PR target: bench harness refactor).
3) Draft a one-pager for sales explaining tradeoffs (p50/p90 vs p99) with 3 recommended presets: "cost-lite", "interactive", "tail-protect".

APPENDIX: quick example console tooltip language (for product copy)
"Tail-protect keeps response time steady during short spikes by combining small prefetches and conservative admission; cost higher than aggressive quantization but reduces bad-experience p99 events."
